l: exemplar guider, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: The exemplar guider is a guider for commit message generation. It learns semantic similarity between an input or current code diff and a retrieved code diff, uses that value to weight the input code diff and retrieved commit message representations, concatenates the code diff with the similar commit message representation, and guides decoding of a commit message.

l: semantic similarity, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: is_between retrieved similar commit [and the current code diff] Semantic similarity between code diffs is represented through encoder outputs and their mean-pooled vectors. The generation module also learns a similarity value between the input and retrieved code diffs with a sigmoid-based exemplar guider.

l: generation of commit message, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: is_guided_by exemplar guider [using semantic similarity] RACE uses the retrieved similar commit as an exemplar for the generation of an accurate commit message. The exemplar guider directs this generation according to the semantic similarity between code diffs.

l: commit message generation dataset, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: A large public dataset of about 0.9 million code-diff and commit-message pairs across five programming languages, used to train an encoder-decoder neural network with retrieval and generation modules.

l: programming languages, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: The experiments cover five programming languages. The paper notes that models perform differently across programming languages and that further experiments are needed to confirm the framework's generality.

l: baseline approaches, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: Baseline approaches are a group comprising IR-based, end-to-end neural, hybrid, and pre-trained-based approaches; they are compared with RACE, which performs best across five programming languages and four evaluation metrics.

l: Seq2Seq-based neural network models, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: Seq2Seq-based neural network models understand code diffs to generate commit messages, but produce high-frequency repetitive tokens; RACE boosts performance.

l: source code, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: is_frequently_changed frequently [in software development and maintenance] It is frequently changed during software development and maintenance.

l: code changes, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: Code changes are often documented by natural language commit messages, but massive changes can be hard to summarize concisely; similar changes help information-retrieval methods and RACE infer a current change’s content and intent.

l: developers, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: experience extra workload [when writing concise and informative messages for massive code changes] They use high-quality commit messages to understand the evolution of software without examining implementation details.

l: software, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: Its evolution can be understood by developers through high-quality commit messages without requiring them to dive into implementation details.

l: information retrieval, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: An information-retrieval approach to commit-message generation finds similar code changes and reuses their messages. Early work uses syntax, semantic, or bag-of-words similarity and BLEU-based selection; evaluated IR approaches, including NNGen and Lucene, generally outperform end-to-end neural models because retrieved similar commits provide important generation information.

l: code diff encoder, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: Code diff encoder trains with a decoder in a commit message generator, learning semantic diff representations mean-pooled into vectors for cosine-similarity retrieval.

l: retrieval-augmented neural commit message generation method, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: The retrieval-augmented neural commit message generation model retrieves similar code diffs and commit messages during training, encodes them, and treats the closest commit message as an exemplar to guide generation of accurate, readable messages. Applied to NMTGen, CommitBERT, CodeT5-small, and CodeT5-base, it boosts performance and outperforms recent baselines. It requires a code base, inherits this IR-based limitation, and has approximately 35 hours of training time.

l: MCMD, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: MCMD is a large-scale dataset for evaluating RACE across Java, C#, C++, Python, and JavaScript. It draws commits from the top-100 starred GitHub repositories for each language, retaining 450,000 randomly sampled commits per language after removing redundant and noisy messages. The study then excludes multi-file commits and unparseable files, compares results with 11 approaches, and reports significantly better RACE performance on four metrics.

l: Java, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: is_a programming language On Java, RACE obtains 25.66 BLEU, 15.46 Meteor, 32.02 Rouge-L, and 1.76 Cider, exceeding the evaluated baselines on all four metrics.

l: C#, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: is_a programming language On C#, RACE obtains 26.33 BLEU, 16.37 Meteor, 31.31 Rouge-L, and 1.84 Cider, exceeding the evaluated baselines on all four metrics.

l: C++, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: is_a programming language On C++, RACE obtains 19.13 BLEU, 12.55 Meteor, 24.52 Rouge-L, and 1.14 Cider, exceeding the evaluated baselines on all four metrics.

l: Python, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: is_a programming language On Python, RACE obtains 21.79 BLEU, 14.68 Meteor, 28.35 Rouge-L, and 1.40 Cider, exceeding the evaluated baselines on all four metrics.

l: JavaScript, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: is_a programming language On JavaScript, RACE obtains 25.55 BLEU, 16.31 Meteor, 31.79 Rouge-L, and 1.84 Cider, exceeding the evaluated baselines on all four metrics.

l: NMTGen, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: NMTGen is a Seq2Seq-based, end-to-end neural network model used as a baseline. It is evaluated against RACE, which enhances it and outperforms it across all human-evaluation aspects. RACE raises NMTGen’s BLEU by over 20% for every programming language and improves average BLEU, Meteor, Rouge-L, and Cider.

l: CommitBERT, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: CommitBERT is a pre-trained Seq2Seq model and hybrid baseline for commit message generation. It uses CodeBERT to learn semantic representations of code diffs and a Transformer-based decoder to generate messages. Fine-tuned on MCMD, it is evaluated as a pre-trained baseline and adapted to RACE, where it improves by 11% BLEU, 9% Meteor, 11% Rouge-L, and 12% Cider, though RACE scores higher on informativeness, conciseness, and expressiveness.

l: CodeT5-base, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: CodeT5-base is a pre-trained Seq2Seq-based model fine-tuned on the commit message generation dataset. It supplies encoder weights for code diff encoders and its decoder for the model. Its 32,100-word vocabulary is expanded by nine special tokens to 32,109. It is the best pre-trained baseline on average before RACE, which improves its average BLEU, Meteor, Rouge-L, and Cider results.

l: BLEU, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: BLEU is an evaluation metric used among four metrics for generated commit messages. A selected variant, B-Norm, is reported to correlate most with human perception. In comparisons across five programming languages, RACE attains the highest BLEU scores and improves adapted models’ average BLEU scores.

l: Meteor, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: is_a evaluation metric Meteor is used to evaluate the quality of generated commit messages.

l: Rouge-L, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: is_a evaluation metric Rouge-L is used to evaluate the quality of generated commit messages.

l: Cider, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: is_a evaluation metric Cider is used to evaluate the quality of generated commit messages.

l: human evaluation, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: Human evaluation, following Moreno et al. (2013), Panichella et al. (2016), and Shi et al. (2021b), randomly samples 50 testing-set code diffs and scores 250 code-diff/commit-message pairs from RACE and four baselines. Four volunteers rate semantic similarity through informativeness, conciseness, and expressiveness; their average scores show high agreement and confirm RACE effectiveness.

l: code intelligence, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: Code intelligence uses machine learning, especially deep learning-based methods, to understand source code. It has produced promising results in tasks including code summarization, code search, and commit message generation.

l: NNGen, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: NNGen is a simple retrieval-based, IR-based baseline model for code diffs. It represents diffs as bag-of-words vectors, uses cosine similarity and nearest neighbors to retrieve messages, and generally outperforms Lucene and end-to-end neural models, though retrieved messages can add incorrect information. RACE surpasses it in human-rated informativeness, conciseness, and expressiveness.

l: cosine similarity, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: measures semantic similarity [between two code diffs] Cosine similarity measures the similarity between pooled semantic vectors produced by the code diff encoder. The retrieval module uses it to rank candidate code diffs in the large parallel training corpus.

l: CodeBERT, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: CodeBERT is described as a pre-trained language model for source code. CommitBERT uses it to learn semantic representations of code diffs.

l: Transformer, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: Transformer-based encoders are used to capture long-range dependencies and contextual information in code diffs. Their layers include multi-head self-attention, relative position embeddings, feed-forward networks, and add-and-norm operations.

l: retrieval-augmented generation, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: uses retrieved relevant results [during training in generation tasks] Introducing retrieved relevant results into the training process has been found useful in many generation tasks. In commit message generation, hybrid approaches combine retrieval with neural generation, although the reviewed methods do not fully exploit retrieved results.

l: ATOM, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: ATOM is a hybrid model combining neural and IR techniques for commit messages. It encodes AST paths from code diffs with BiLSTM, generates messages with a decoder, retrieves messages via TF-IDF and cosine similarity, then hybrid-ranks both results without refining them.

l: CoRec, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: CoRec is a hybrid, pre-trained-based model that combines neural and IR-based approaches for message generation. During inference only, it uses a trained encoder to retrieve the most similar training code diff, combines decoder probability distributions for the input and retrieved diff, and generates a message step by step; it is not trained to use retrieved information. It outperforms NNGen on C++ and JavaScript but trails it on Java, C#, and Python, while RACE surpasses it on all human-evaluation aspects.

l: exemplar-based commit message generation, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: An approach that retrieves similar commits as exemplars and trains a model to leverage them, enhancing commit message generation.

l: retrieval module, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: The retrieval module trains a code diff encoder with a commit message generator, maps code diffs into a high-dimensional semantic space, measures cosine similarity, and searches a large parallel training corpus. It retrieves the most similar code diff and its paired commit message, using the second-ranked training result because the first is itself.

l: generation module, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: The generation module combines input code-diff and retrieved-information representations using three Transformer-based encoders, an exemplar guider, and a decoder to generate a commit message.

l: large parallel training corpus, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: The large parallel training corpus contains paired code diffs and commit messages. The retrieval module searches this corpus for the most semantically similar code diff and its paired commit message.

l: decoder, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: Transformer-based decoder generates commit messages step by step from combined input encoding, using masked self-attention, cross-attention, feed-forward networks, and softmax token probabilities; trained with cross-entropy and AdamW.

l: commits, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: MCMD contains commit code diffs, messages, repository names, timestamps, and other information; the study filters out multiple-file and unparsable-file commits.

l: token-level change actions, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: Token-level change actions represent code changes through keep, insert, delete, and replace; replace splits into replace_old and replace_new, while difflib extracts action sequences from Experimental Setup / Dataset through Evaluation metrics / Baselines.

l: B-Norm, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: is_a BLEU variant [used in this paper] B-Norm is the BLEU result reported in the study. It is selected from BLEU variants because it correlates most closely with human perception according to Tao et al. (2021).

l: Lucene, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: Lucene is a traditional IR-based baseline using TF-IDF to represent code diffs; it generally performs below NNGen, retrieving relevant meaning but sometimes adding incorrect content.

l: CodeT5-small, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: CodeT5-small is a Seq2Seq-based, source code pre-trained model fine-tuned on commit message generation data and MCMD as a comparison baseline. It performs below CodeT5-base among pre-trained approaches, then gains 15% BLEU, 14% Meteor, 11% Rouge-L, and 26% Cider when enhanced with RACE.

l: pre-trained-based approaches, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: outperform baseline approaches [on average across four metrics] Pre-trained-based approaches outperform the other baseline categories on average across the four metrics. CodeT5-base performs best among the evaluated pre-trained-based approaches before applying RACE.

l: Informativeness, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: measures important information about the code diff reflected in the commit message Informativeness measures the amount of important information about the code diff reflected in a commit message. RACE performs better than the other approaches on this aspect.

l: Conciseness, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: measures extraneous information included in the commit message Conciseness measures the extent of extraneous information included in a commit message. RACE performs better than the other approaches on this aspect.

l: Expressiveness, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: measures grammaticality and fluency Expressiveness measures grammaticality and fluency. RACE performs better than the other approaches on this aspect.

l: Table 3, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: Table 3 presents human evaluation scores and standard deviations for informativeness, conciseness, and expressiveness across five models.

l: volunteers, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: Four volunteers with excellent English and over three years of software development experience score code diff–commit message pairs, averaging their evaluations into each final score.

l: semantic similarity, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: Semantic similarity is the target of the human evaluation of generated commit messages. The evaluation indicates that RACE produces messages with more comprehensive semantics than the four baselines.

l: Krippendorff’s alpha, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: has_value 0.90 [agreement among volunteers] Krippendorff’s alpha is calculated to verify agreement among the volunteers. Its value is 0.90, indicating a high degree of agreement and reliable scores.

l: Kendall’s Tau, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: has_value 0.73 to 0.95 [pairwise values among volunteers] Kendall’s Tau is calculated pairwise among the four volunteers to assess agreement. The pairwise values range from 0.73 to 0.95, indicating high agreement.

l: Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: Wilcoxon signed-rank tests confirm RACE’s superiority in human evaluation, with statistically significant improvements over other approaches and all p-values below 0.05 at 95% confidence.

l: code base, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: The method requires a code base from which it retrieves the most similar example. This requirement is identified as a limitation inherited from information-retrieval-based techniques.

l: training time, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: The model takes about 35 hours to train because it retrieves similar diffs and encodes them in addition to modeling the input code diffs.

l: research work, RACE: Retrieval-Augmented Commit Message Generation
s: The research work received valuable comments from reviewers. It was supported, but the text does not specify the source or nature of that support.
